BR_1_BACKUP_AND_RESTORE.registerDefinition: No evidence exists of a tested backup or a rehearsed restore for the production database or object storage.
BR_1_BACKUP_AND_RESTORE.registerEvidenceClaimWasWrong: The register recorded 'no restore evidence in verification/'. §269 had already taken a full logical backup and rehearsed a restore (76/76 tables, 7049/7049 rows). §289 did it again, freshly and more strictly.
BR_1_BACKUP_AND_RESTORE.backupMechanism: operator-controlled logical backup via pg_dump against the DIRECT Neon endpoint; independent of the Neon console
BR_1_BACKUP_AND_RESTORE.clientRequired: PostgreSQL 17+. The local postgresql@16 client refuses the 17.11 server; /opt/homebrew/opt/libpq/bin/pg_dump 18.3 was used.

restoreRehearsal.target: disposable PostgreSQL 17.11 container — an exact production server-version match
restoreRehearsal.integrityMethod: per-table md5 over per-row md5s, ordered COLLATE "C" so the comparison does not depend on the two servers' differing collations

BR_1_BACKUP_AND_RESTORE.collationTrap: A first attempt ordered by row text and reported the `user` table as differing. Per-row hashes were identical: Neon runs lc_collate=C.UTF-8 and the container en_US.utf8, so the same rows concatenated in a different order. Recorded because it will recur on any future rehearsal.
BR_1_BACKUP_AND_RESTORE.notEstablished: Neon's control plane was unreachable (no NEON_* credential). Platform retention window and point-in-time-recovery setting are UNREAD. Registered as BR-2.
BR_1_BACKUP_AND_RESTORE.verdict: CLOSED for Threshold A — a backup was taken from live production and a restore was verified by content, not by row count.

pendingMigrations.name: ExpertAnalysisAuthorityFoundation
pendingMigrations.upOperations: 4 columns on hazlenz_analyses (all DEFAULTed or NULLable), new table expert_analysis_executions, 4 indexes, 6 constraints, 1 backfill UPDATE
pendingMigrations.backfillEffect: sets producer='client_supplied', analysisState='ANALYSIS_AVAILABLE', confirmationRequired=false on existing rows. Rehearsal confirmed all 8 production rows take exactly these values.
pendingMigrations.applicationCompatibility: old code tolerates it — added columns are not selected by the pre-019000 entity and are defaulted
pendingMigrations.downNote: drops the table and four columns; does NOT self-enforce; must never run against a database that has served beta traffic

pendingMigrations.name: ExpertHumanConfirmation
pendingMigrations.upOperations: widens human_reviews.decision varchar(24)->(32), replaces its CHECK, adds nullable settlementReviewId, 2 partial unique indexes
pendingMigrations.preflight: PASS — 0 duplicate groups would violate uq_human_review_analysis_settlement; the single existing decision value 'accepted' is permitted by the new CHECK; varchar widening is metadata-only in PostgreSQL
pendingMigrations.downNote: SELF-ENFORCING: refuses outright if any analysis references a settlement. Its DELETE removes only rows whose decision could not have existed before the migration, so it destroys no pre-existing data.
pendingMigrations.applicationCompatibility: backward compatible — widening a column and adding permitted enum values

pendingMigrations.name: ProducerScopedAnalysisCurrentness
pendingMigrations.upOperations: creates uq_hazlenz_analysis_current_by_producer (observationId, producer) WHERE status='current'; drops uq_hazlenz_analysis_current
pendingMigrations.downNote: SELF-ENFORCING in practice: recreating the stricter index fails on any observation carrying both a current deterministic and a current Expert analysis. Production has none, so the rehearsal succeeded.
pendingMigrations.applicationCompatibility: relaxes a constraint; rolling application code back past §267 while it remains reintroduces the §266 P0-2 selection defect for the duration of the rollback

pendingMigrations.name: CorrectiveActionLifecycle
pendingMigrations.upOperations: 3 nullable columns on corrective_actions (closedAt, closedByUserId, clientRequestId), 1 partial unique index, 1 composite index
pendingMigrations.preflight: PASS — table has 1 row, none with a clientRequestId
pendingMigrations.downNote: drops the three columns; no self-enforcement, but they carry no data before the migration

DB_3_OUTCOMES_TABLE_FINDING.registerClaim: The outcomes table is deliberately absent from the migration set, which keeps the cross-tenant recurrence code unreachable.
DB_3_OUTCOMES_TABLE_FINDING.halfThatIsTrue: No migration in the candidate creates `outcomes`. Verified by grep across all 54 migration files: zero references.
DB_3_OUTCOMES_TABLE_FINDING.halfThatIsFalse: The `outcomes` table EXISTS in production — 13 columns, 0 rows. It is one of the 76 tables in the backup. No migration creates it, so it predates the migration set, most plausibly from a period when TYPEORM_SYNCHRONIZE was enabled.
DB_3_OUTCOMES_TABLE_FINDING.consequence: The containment argument written into corrective-actions.service.ts — 'NO MIGRATION CREATES THE TABLE ... so the table cannot appear by any other route' — does not hold in production. On production, closing a corrective action will NOT fail with 'relation outcomes does not exist'. It will succeed, write an outcome row, and run OutcomeService.checkRecurrence, which applies no organization or owner scope.
DB_3_OUTCOMES_TABLE_FINDING.evidenceOfScope: OutcomeService.checkRecurrence counts by category across every tenant; the Outcome entity carries no tenantId or organizationId column. The one caller is CorrectiveActionsService.recordClosureIntelligence, reached from PATCH /actions/:id/status with statusCode 'closed'.

materialityByThreshold.A: NOT MATERIAL — no users, so no closure occurs.
materialityByThreshold.B: NOT a cross-tenant leak with a single owner tenant, but auto-escalation to 'urgent' on the owner's own history would fire silently, which is the undecided D-055 product question.
materialityByThreshold.C: MATERIAL — one customer's action would be escalated on another customer's history.

DB_3_OUTCOMES_TABLE_FINDING.containment: NOT CONTAINED in production by the mechanism the register and the code rely on.
DB_3_OUTCOMES_TABLE_FINDING.secondConsequence: All §286 and §287 action-closure evidence was gathered against databases WITHOUT the outcomes table. Local closure evidence therefore does not represent production closure behaviour.
DB_3_OUTCOMES_TABLE_FINDING.action: Registered as DB-4 (P1, blocks C) and TI-2's stated basis corrected. Not repaired in §289: repairing it is either a tenant-scoping change to the recurrence query or a product decision about whether the outcome loop is per-tenant or global, and neither is release engineering.
